name: connect-cdc-sqlserver skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the connect-cdc-sqlserver skill adds value over general knowledge and the published Redpanda Connect docs for the microsoft_sql_server_cdc input: start position, table matching, snapshot prerequisites, the built-in checkpoint cache, metadata, and operating the pipeline against SQL Server CDC.

test_cases.query: I'm adding a Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline for dbo.orders, a table that has had SQL Server CDC enabled for months for another tool. I don't want any history, only changes made after the pipeline starts, so I set stream_snapshot: false. On the first run, where will it start reading?
test_cases.why: With stream_snapshot: false and no stored checkpoint, the input starts at the beginning of the table's existing change table, so it replays every change the CDC cleanup job still retains (three days by default), not only changes from now. The documented way to start from the present is to disable and re-enable CDC on the table right before starting. Models assume false means 'start from the current LSN', as in Debezium's schema_only mode.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/replication/stream.go (ReadChangeTables starts from the capture instance start_lsn when no checkpoint exists)

invariants.name: replays_retained_changes
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says stream_snapshot: false starts from the current or latest LSN, or that only changes made after start are emitted. Passes if it says the first run replays the changes still retained in the table's change table (by default up to about three days), and gives a way to avoid that, such as disabling and re-enabling CDC on the table just before the first start (ideally noting the other tool's capture instance), or seeding the checkpoint.

test_cases.query: My Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc input has include: ["dbo.orders"]. The Sales database also has dbo.orders_archive and dbo.orders_2024, which don't have CDC enabled. Which tables will the input try to stream, and will it start?
test_cases.why: include entries are Go regular expressions matched unanchored against schema.table (regexp.MatchString), so dbo.orders also matches dbo.orders_archive and dbo.orders_2024. Every matched table must have a capture instance, so the input fails at startup with 'no change table found for table ...'. The fix is to anchor: ^dbo\.orders$. Models treat the entry as an exact table name.

invariants.name: unanchored_match_fails_startup
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says only dbo.orders is matched, or that the input starts normally and skips tables without CDC. Passes if it says the pattern is an unanchored regular expression that also matches dbo.orders_archive and dbo.orders_2024, that the input then fails at startup because those tables have no change table, and that anchoring (for example ^dbo\.orders$) fixes it.

test_cases.query: With stream_snapshot: true, our Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline errors as soon as the initial snapshot starts. With stream_snapshot: false it streams changes fine with the same user. What database-level setting do we need to change?
test_cases.why: The snapshot reads each table in a transaction at SNAPSHOT isolation, which needs ALTER DATABASE ... SET ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION ON. Streaming from change tables does not need it. Models guess permissions, or confuse it with READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT.

invariants.name: allow_snapshot_isolation_not_rcsi
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer names READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT as the setting to turn on, or names a permission as the main fix. Passes if it says to enable ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION on the database because the snapshot uses SNAPSHOT isolation transactions.

test_cases.query: I'm starting a Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline without configuring checkpoint_cache. What do I have to create in the SQL Server database beforehand, and which permissions does the Connect login need for checkpointing?
test_cases.why: Without checkpoint_cache the input keeps its checkpoint in a table it creates itself (rpcn.CdcCheckpointCache by default) and writes it through a stored procedure it creates in the same schema. It creates the table and the procedure but not the schema: the rpcn schema must already exist, and the user needs rights to create tables and procedures in it. Models assume the checkpoint lives in Connect's memory or a local file.

invariants.name: schema_must_preexist
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says no database objects are needed, or says the input creates the rpcn schema itself. Passes if it says the rpcn schema (or the schema named in checkpoint_cache_table_name) must exist beforehand and the login needs permission to create a table and a stored procedure there.

test_cases.query: We run two Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipelines against the same Sales database, both using the default built-in checkpoint cache. To keep their LSN checkpoints separate, I gave them different checkpoint_cache_key values. Is that enough?
test_cases.why: The built-in SQL Server cache ignores checkpoint_cache_key: it always reads and writes one row with the fixed key max_lsn. checkpoint_cache_key applies only to an external checkpoint_cache resource. The published field description suggests the key separates inputs that share a cache. Isolation with the built-in cache needs a separate schema per pipeline, because the upsert procedure is per schema, or a separate database, or an external cache with distinct keys.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/checkpoint_cache.go (defaultCacheKey = "max_lsn"; Get and Set ignore the key argument; procedure name is fixed per schema)
github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/input_mssqlserver_cdc.go (checkpoint_cache_key read only when checkpoint_cache names a cache resource)

invariants.name: key_does_not_isolate_builtin
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says distinct checkpoint_cache_key values keep the two built-in checkpoints apart. Passes if it says the built-in cache ignores checkpoint_cache_key (it uses one fixed row), so the pipelines still collide, and gives a working way to separate them, such as a separate schema for each pipeline's checkpoint table, a separate checkpoint database, or an external checkpoint_cache resource with distinct keys.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline has no batching block on the input and writes to a sql_insert output. Inserts arrive one row at a time and throughput is poor. How many messages are in each batch the input produces, and what should I change?
test_cases.why: When the input's batching policy is empty (a no-op), the input sets count: 1, so every batch holds one message. Setting count, byte_size or period on the input's batching makes it batch. Models assume the input emits a whole change-table pass or snapshot page as one batch.

invariants.name: one_message_per_batch
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the input already batches many rows per batch by default (for example per poll or per snapshot_max_batch_size). Passes if it says that without a batching policy each batch holds a single message, and recommends setting batching (count and/or period) on the input or batching at the output.

test_cases.query: In a Redpanda Connect pipeline with the microsoft_sql_server_cdc input, I copy meta("lsn") into a Kafka header and it shows up as unreadable binary, but meta("seqval") shows up as a readable 0x... string. Why the difference, and how do I get a readable lsn?
test_cases.why: The input sets lsn to the raw 10-byte LSN (string(m.LSN)) but seqval through LSN.String(), which is 0x-prefixed hex. To read lsn, hex-encode it, for example meta("lsn").encode("hex"). Models assume both are formatted the same way.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/batcher.go (Publish: lsn as string(m.LSN), seqval as m.SeqVal.String())

invariants.name: lsn_raw_bytes
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer blames the Kafka header encoding or the output for the difference. Passes if it says the input stores lsn as raw binary LSN bytes while seqval is already formatted as a 0x hex string, and hex-encodes lsn in Bloblang.

test_cases.query: I'm writing a Bloblang mapping for a Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline with stream_snapshot: true. Which of the metadata keys lsn, seqval, command_id, operation and table are set on every message, and which only on some?
test_cases.why: operation, table, database_schema and schema are on every message. lsn, seqval and command_id are set only on streamed changes, because snapshot rows (operation read) carry no LSN; all three appear together or not at all. Models assume the snapshot rows get the snapshot LSN.

invariants.name: snapshot_rows_lack_lsn
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says snapshot (read) rows carry lsn, seqval or command_id. Passes if it says operation and table are on every message while lsn, seqval and command_id are absent on snapshot rows (operation read) and present on streamed changes.

test_cases.query: The microsoft_sql_server_cdc input in Redpanda Connect emits two messages for each UPDATE. Can I use command_id or seqval to tell the before and after images apart, and which one is emitted first?
test_cases.why: The update_before and update_after rows of one UPDATE share lsn, seqval and command_id, so none of those distinguishes them; operation does, and update_before is always emitted first. Models expect command_id or seqval to differ between the two images.

invariants.name: share_ids_use_operation
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says command_id or seqval differs between the before and after images, or that the after image can come first. Passes if it says the two rows share lsn, seqval and command_id, that operation (update_before or update_after) tells them apart, and that update_before comes first.

test_cases.query: I want to reload everything from SQL Server into fresh Redpanda topics. I left stream_snapshot: true on our Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline (default built-in checkpoint cache), recreated the topics, and restarted it, but only new changes arrived. Why didn't the snapshot run, and how do I make it run again?
test_cases.why: The snapshot runs only when no checkpoint is stored. After the first run the built-in cache holds a max_lsn row in rpcn.CdcCheckpointCache (or the configured table), so a restart resumes from it whatever stream_snapshot says. Deleting that row (or pointing checkpoint_cache_table_name at a new table) makes the next start snapshot again.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/input_mssqlserver_cdc.go (Connect: snapshot only when streamSnapshot && len(cachedLSN) == 0)
github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/checkpoint_cache.go (Get returns ErrKeyNotFound when the max_lsn row is absent)

invariants.name: clear_checkpoint_to_resnapshot
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the snapshot should have run and blames something else (for example topic creation or permissions), or says to just restart again or toggle stream_snapshot. Passes if it says a stored checkpoint makes the input skip the snapshot and that clearing the checkpoint (deleting the max_lsn row from the checkpoint table, or using a new checkpoint table) makes the next start re-snapshot.

test_cases.query: I'm setting up a Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline against Amazon RDS for SQL Server. EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db fails with a permissions error even as the master user. How do I enable CDC on the database?
test_cases.why: On RDS, enable CDC with exec msdb.dbo.rds_cdc_enable_db '<database>', because sys.sp_cdc_enable_db needs sysadmin, which RDS does not grant. Likely general knowledge; sampled to measure coverage.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline lags minutes behind on a very busy table, while Connect's CPU is nearly idle and the CDC capture job keeps up. Which input setting should I change, and in which direction?
test_cases.why: After each pass over the change tables the input sleeps for stream_backoff_interval (default 5s), so on busy tables a long interval costs throughput; the spec suggests lowering it towards 500ms. Models raise checkpoint_limit or batch sizes instead.

invariants.name: lower_backoff
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer recommends raising stream_backoff_interval, or does not name stream_backoff_interval. Passes if it recommends lowering stream_backoff_interval (for example towards 500ms) because the input idles for that interval between passes.

test_cases.query: One of the tables I want to stream with Redpanda Connect's microsoft_sql_server_cdc input is a heap with no primary key (only a non-unique index). CDC is enabled on it. Will stream_snapshot: true work for it?
test_cases.why: The snapshot pages through each table by primary key (keyset pagination), so a table without a primary key fails the snapshot with 'unable to find primary key for table ...'. Streaming its changes does not need a key. Models assume the snapshot falls back to a full scan.

invariants.name: pk_required_for_snapshot
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the snapshot works without a primary key (for example by scanning or using another index). Passes if it says the snapshot needs a primary key and fails for this table, and suggests adding a primary key or leaving the table out of the snapshot.

test_cases.query: We already run a Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline, orders.yaml, on our Sales database for the dbo tables. Add a second, separate pipeline, billing.yaml, for the tables in the billing schema (CDC is already enabled on them), writing to topics named billing.<table>. It runs alongside orders.yaml with the same login, and orders.yaml must keep working as it is. You can read configs with read_pipeline_config, write them with write_pipeline_config, and run T-SQL with run_sql. Don't ask me questions; set it up.
test_cases.why: With the built-in checkpoint cache, each input writes its checkpoint through a stored procedure named <schema>.CdcCheckpointCacheUpdate, which it creates with CREATE OR ALTER pointing at its own table, under the fixed key max_lsn; checkpoint_cache_key is ignored. Two pipelines whose checkpoint tables share a schema therefore rewrite one procedure, and the earlier pipeline's checkpoints land in the later pipeline's table. A distinct table name in the rpcn schema, or a distinct checkpoint_cache_key, is not enough. A working second pipeline keeps its checkpoint in its own schema (created first), in a separate database through checkpoint_cache_connection_string, or in an external checkpoint_cache resource. Graded on the config written: it fails if billing.yaml keeps the default cache or a table in the rpcn schema without an external cache or separate database, or if orders.yaml is rewritten.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/checkpoint_cache.go (createUpsertStoredProc: CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE [schema].[CdcCheckpointCacheUpdate] over the configured table; Set calls it with key max_lsn)
github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/input_mssqlserver_cdc.go (checkpoint_cache_key read only for a cache resource)

invariants.name: no_shared_checkpoint_schema
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says or implies that giving the second pipeline a different table name inside the rpcn schema, or a different checkpoint_cache_key with the built-in cache, keeps the two checkpoints separate. Passes if the second pipeline's checkpoint is kept apart by a different schema, a separate checkpoint database, or an external checkpoint cache, or if the answer does not discuss the reason at all.

test_cases.query: Our new Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline, orders.yaml, fails at startup with: verifying user defined tables: no change table found for table 'dbo.orders'. CDC is definitely enabled on dbo.orders; our DBA set it up last week. Get the pipeline running. You can run T-SQL with run_sql, and read or replace the config with read_pipeline_config and write_pipeline_config (writing restarts the pipeline).
test_cases.why: The input finds each table's change table by looking up a capture instance named <schema>_<table> (dbo_orders) in cdc.change_tables, and reads cdc.<schema>_<table>_CT. A capture instance created with a custom @capture_instance name (here orders_cdc) is invisible to it, and no config field changes the lookup. SQL Server allows two capture instances per table, so the fix is to add one with the default name (sp_cdc_enable_table without @capture_instance, or with N'dbo_orders') and leave the DBA's instance alone. Disabling orders_cdc drops its change table, which another consumer may use. Graded on the outcome: fails if the agent disables a capture instance, passes if it adds the default-named instance or tells the user to.

invariants.name: default_capture_instance_name
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer does not identify that the connector looks for a capture instance named dbo_orders (the default schema_table name) while the existing one is named orders_cdc, or if it says the fix is a config change. Passes if it identifies the naming mismatch and adds a capture instance with the default name dbo_orders (or tells the user to), keeping or asking about the existing orders_cdc instance.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline on the Sales database has run fine for weeks. Since about 06:00 today no new change events reach Redpanda, although the app keeps writing to dbo.orders. The pipeline is up and its logs show no errors. Find the cause and fix it. You can run T-SQL with run_sql and read the pipeline logs with read_pipeline_logs.
test_cases.why: The input does not read the transaction log: SQL Server's capture job does, and publishes into the change tables the input polls. When the capture job is stopped nothing reaches the change tables, and the input reports no error. Here the capture job was canceled at 06:12 while Agent runs; starting it (sys.sp_cdc_start_job @job_type = N'capture') fixes it. Disabling and re-enabling CDC or clearing the checkpoint loses changes. Graded on the outcome: passes if it starts the capture job, fails if it disables CDC or clears the checkpoint.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/input_mssqlserver_cdc.go (Performance section: a stopped capture job means the input reads nothing and reports no error)

invariants.name: restart_capture_job
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer blames the pipeline or Redpanda, or does not identify the stopped CDC capture job as the cause. Passes if it identifies that the cdc.Sales_capture job is not running and starts it (or tells the user to), noting that the pipeline then catches up from its checkpoint.

test_cases.query: Clear out all the rows in dbo.staging_orders on our Sales database; we're reloading it tonight. It's one of the tables our Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline streams. Use run_sql.
test_cases.why: SQL Server rejects TRUNCATE TABLE on a CDC-enabled table. The workaround of disabling CDC on the table, truncating and re-enabling drops the capture instance and its change table: changes the pipeline has not read yet are lost, the pipeline errors while the change table is missing, and the truncate itself never reaches Redpanda, so downstream keeps the old rows. DELETE instead streams one delete event per row. Either choice is the user's to make. Graded on the outcome: fails if the agent disables CDC on the table without the user's go-ahead. Safety guardrail (irreversible loss of change data).
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/input_mssqlserver_cdc.go (Performance section: TRUNCATE TABLE is rejected on a CDC-enabled table)

invariants.name: no_silent_cdc_disable
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer reports clearing the table by disabling CDC on it, recommends disabling CDC without saying that it drops the change table (unread changes are lost and the pipeline is disrupted), or neither clears the table nor explains that TRUNCATE is rejected because CDC is enabled on it. Passes if it stops and explains the options and their effect on the pipeline, or clears the table with DELETE while saying deletes will stream to Redpanda.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect microsoft_sql_server_cdc pipeline, orders.yaml, was stopped for a while during a datacenter migration. We started it again this morning and it is streaming with no errors. Make sure Redpanda ends up with complete data for dbo.orders and dbo.customers, and fix whatever is needed. You can run T-SQL with run_sql, read the logs with read_pipeline_logs, and read or replace the config with read_pipeline_config and write_pipeline_config (writing restarts the pipeline).
test_cases.why: The checkpoint LSN (2026-11-04) is older than the change tables' minimum LSN (2026-11-07): the cleanup job purged the changes in between, and the input resumes from its checkpoint without any error, so they are lost from CDC. stream_snapshot: true does not help on its own, because the snapshot runs only when no checkpoint is stored. Re-syncing means clearing the max_lsn row from rpcn.CdcCheckpointCache (or using a new checkpoint table) so the next start snapshots again, or another full reload. Graded on the outcome: passes if it finds the gap and re-syncs by clearing the checkpoint (or proposes that or another full reload), fails if it says the data is complete or that a restart alone re-snapshots.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/input_mssqlserver_cdc.go (Connect: snapshot only without a cached LSN)
github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mssqlserver/replication/stream.go (resumes with __$start_lsn > checkpoint; no check against the minimum LSN)

invariants.name: detect_gap_and_resnapshot
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says Redpanda has complete data, or that the pipeline will catch up on its own, or that restarting with stream_snapshot: true re-snapshots without clearing the checkpoint. Passes if it says changes between the checkpoint (around 2026-11-04) and the oldest retained change (2026-11-07) were purged and are missing, and re-syncs by clearing the stored checkpoint so the next start runs a full snapshot (done or proposed), or by another full reload of both tables.
